_comment_ui: In-sim overlays, both off here so the sim opens straight onto the car. MissionControl.Panel = the Mission Control panel on Tab; Menu.Enabled = the main menu (Manual / Autonomous / Track editor) the sim opens on. Set either to true to turn it on. Left out of settings.json, both are on.
_comment_plant: Which implementation of IFSDSPlant stands behind the car. 'chaos' = Chaos observes the car it is already integrating (the only validated reference). 'shadow' = Chaos still DRIVES and the FMU is stepped alongside it with identical inputs, with divergence logged once a second; behaviour is unchanged by construction because nothing downstream reads the shadow. 'fmu' = the FMU is the plant, but the pawn is still Chaos-integrated, so the sensors describe a different car from the one on screen — bring-up only until the Phase 6 kinematic swap. See docs/fmu_plant_migration.md.

Plant._comment_shadowsync: Force the shadow's PLANAR state (x, y, yaw and the planar velocities) equal to the reference's every step, so the comparison asks 'same state, same inputs, same response?' instead of 'how far apart do they drift?'. The drift question cannot be answered by an open-loop shadow at all — the controller is steering the reference, so the shadow diverges without bound however good it is. Vertical state is deliberately NOT synced: the two plants do not share a ride-height convention and the suspension is 56,900 N/m per corner, so injecting the reference's z inflates Fz, inflates mu*Fz with it, and produced 12-14 g of phantom lateral force. Set false only to watch a shadow run free, which is a demo rather than a measurement.

_comment_environment: Trackside environment (docs/ENVIRONMENT_ROADMAP.md). When Enabled, loading a track also loads the <track>.env.json sidecar next to its CSV: ground extent and props, generated in Python from a seed and a profile (docs/environment_sidecar.md). Off by default so the flat world stays the regression baseline; while off, a sidecar is ignored, except a venue track's (profile venue_<venue>, docs/venues.md), which always loads.

FSCar._comment_mesh: The art the car is drawn with: the IFS-08, generated from the team's Blender livery scene by tools/assetgen (docs/vehicle_art.md). Body is a skeletal mesh with bones WheelFL/FR/RL/RR at the hub centres and its origin on the ground under the centre of mass; Wheels (what spins) and Corners (upright and caliper) are posed every tick from the plant's wheel state, FL, FR, RL, RR. Only what is drawn: mass, geometry, aero and suspension come from VehiclePhysics. Remove the block, or a Body that does not load, for the inherited Technion car.

VehiclePhysics._comment_motor: MotorMaxTorque, MotorMaxPower, MotorRPM[], MotorTorque[] are vestigial. Drive torque comes from the dedicated UEmraxMotor class (EMRAX 228 MV at 400 V bus, see Plugins/FSDSPlugin/Source/FSDSPlugin/Public/EmraxMotor.h). The pawn silences Chaos's ICE-style engine each tick (SetThrottleInput(0)) and injects per-wheel torque via SetDriveTorque, so these fields feed only the silenced Chaos engine and have no effect on actual driving. Of the motor-side settings, MaxRegenTorque/MaxRegenPower and MotorMaxPower (the drive power cap, 80 kW per the FS rules) are forwarded to the EMRAX class; MotorMaxTorque and the curve arrays are not, peak torque comes from the EMRAX envelope. Kept here so existing tooling and external mirrors keep parsing; remove in a future pass.
VehiclePhysics._comment_regen: Regen is the ONLY braking channel on this car — there is no hydraulic service brake, and EBS is a separate pneumatic system on the handbrake channel. These two therefore define the entire service-deceleration authority of the vehicle. They were previously C++ defaults in FSDSSettings.h with no entry here, which meant the braking model was inheriting numbers nobody had chosen. MaxRegenTorque is the motor-side negative-torque cap; MaxRegenPower is the battery cell input-current limit and is the binding constraint at most speeds. 11000 W is the IFS-08 pack's charge limit: 95s6p Sony VTC6, 5 A max continuous charge per cell (Sony's own standard charge is 3 A; 5 A is the cell's maximum, the cells were not chosen for regen) = 30 A at ~370 V. It was 6000 W, about the 3 A standard charge, which held braking to ~2.5 m/s² at 10 m/s. Near full charge the 4.2 V cell limit allows less, so regen at 100% SoC is lower on the real car.
VehiclePhysics._comment_gear: GearRatio and WheelRadius stay at 2.909 and 0.202 m, not the KIN model's 3.5833 (43/12) and 0.2002 m: the pipeline turns /motor_rpm into speed with 2*pi*0.202/(60*2.909) = 0.00727 m/s per rpm (odometry_filter kRpmToMs, cone_slam RPM_TO_MS), and the sim must generate rpm the same way or every speed the pipeline sees is off (24 % with 43/12). On the car, LiDAR scan registration on the 2026-09-20 manual bag's straights gives about 0.0066 m/s per rpm: with 43/12 that needs a 0.226 m rolling radius, more than the 0.203 m tyre; with 32/11 it is 0.183 m, tyre load and slip below the geometric value. Change both here and in the pipeline together once the car's sprockets are checked.
VehiclePhysics._comment_rolling: Rolling resistance coefficient. Absent until now, which the shadow FMU exposed twice over: a parked FMU car crept at ~1.5 mm/s because nothing opposed motion at zero slip, and on the same throttle that holds Chaos at 3.0 m/s the FMU reached 8.1 m/s mean. The FMU applies it as a resistive WHEEL TORQUE, Crr*Fz*Rw, which is the actual mechanism (contact-patch pressure shifting forward). Chaos has no rolling resistance, so the Chaos plant applies the same Crr*(m*g + downforce) as a body force opposing velocity. 0.020 is typical for a racing slick on warm tarmac; it is an ASSUMPTION, not measured on the IFS-08.
VehiclePhysics._comment_ebs: EBS torque per wheel = EbsGripMultiple * TireMu * (Mass*g/4) * WheelRadius, about 272 N.m, the same formula as matlab/plant/ifssim_params.m. Before this it was the Chaos engine default of 3000 N.m, about 15x the grip limit. EbsFillTime is a linear ramp from 0 to full torque, in seconds; 0 is instant, matching the MATLAB plant. Both are ASSUMPTIONS until measured on the car, and the fill time is the one that decides stopping distance.
VehiclePhysics._comment_inertia: Body inertia about the centre of mass, kg*m^2: roll Ixx, pitch Iyy, yaw Izz. From SOLIDWORKS mass properties of the IFS-08 KIN assembly AS_KIN_CHASSIS (IFS08_KIN cad/_tools/car_inertia.py, 2026-11-26): 221.8 kg, 48.2 % front, CoG ~0.26 m; the sum of its 293 top-level components' own tensors moved to the car's CoG (the whole-assembly query returns no body). Off-diagonal terms < 1 kg*m^2. Not measured: the model is balanced to the weighed 220 kg (car without driver) and 48.1 % front with set masses for the accumulator (50 kg; the rebuilt AS_BT_1000_v2 is 50.6 kg) and a 37.6 kg block for what the CAD lacks (harness, LV, seat, fluids, DV kit...), its inertia a uniform 500 x 300 x 1200 mm box. Cross-check: the Blender density estimate (tools/assetgen/blender/estimate_ifs08_inertia.py -- --total-kg 220 --cells-kg 38) gives [30.3, 104.5, 120.1]. Without it the sim keeps the physics asset's own tensor (the IFS-08's gives 27.9 / 193 / 210 about its principal axes). It is applied only when the asset's principal axes lie along the car's: the Technion car's do not, so on that car it is ignored with an error in the log. Replace with a swing/pendulum test when there is one. matlab/plant reads it from here.
VehiclePhysics._comment_damping: The strut damping ratios that reach Chaos are DampingRatioFront/DampingRatioRear (per axle, from the KIN CAD dampers; ApplyTireModelToWheelCDOs). SuspensionDamping is only the fallback for a settings file without them. Chaos turns the ratio into a damping coefficient (N*s/m) from the spring rate and sprung mass when it builds the car, and the sim log prints the result per wheel ('strut in the solver'). Chaos caps the ratio at 1.0. RoadRoughnessGd0 4.5e-4 was fitted on dev (#959) with a single ratio of 0.7 and the old 20.2 kN/m springs against the 2026-09-20 manual bag; with the CAD dampers and springs the vibration match wants re-fitting.
VehiclePhysics._comment_suspension: Springs per axle from the KIN CAD (wheel rate = spring x motion ratio^2 from the kinematic sweep), no anti-roll bar (RollbarScaling 0, see FSDSWheelFront.cpp). Chaos takes SpringRate*/DampingRatio*/WheelMass* from here (ApplyTireModelToWheelCDOs, droop travel recomputed so the ride height does not move); RollStiffness*/Heave/Pitch feed the shadow load-transfer model. Check against the car: ride 2.7 / 3.1 Hz (plant spec 2.9-3.0), pitch 0.66 deg/g (2026-09-20 manual bag 0.6-0.8), roll 1.1 deg/g driverless, ~1.5 scaled to the bag's driven car (1.5-1.8).
VehiclePhysics._comment_generated: GENERATED from the IFS-08 KIN model (driverless__baseline, 2026-11-15 19:11) by IFS08_KIN/model/generators/ifssim.py. Edit the model (vehicle_params.json / configs / setups), not this block. Fields marked ESTIMATE/KEPT in ifssim_mapping.md are not IFS-08 data yet.
VehiclePhysics._comment_road: Road roughness on the level floor every generated track sits on, and on a track world such as Montmeló, whose asphalt the world generator writes as a smooth fitted surface (RoadRoughnessOnTrackWorld false turns it off on worlds). A random ISO 8608 road profile per wheel track (displacement PSD Gd0 x (n/0.1)^-2, rolled off past CutoffWavelength; the two tracks share their waves longer than CrossWavelength, so long waves lift the car instead of rolling it: drawn independently they rolled it 2x the car at 0.5-3 Hz at 11 m/s), averaged over the tyre Footprint, drives each corner through the tyre's vertical stiffness to the wheel, and the strut passes the wheel's motion to the body with the solver's own spring and damper. Gd0 4.5e-4 m^3 (ISO class C) is fitted with SuspensionDamping 0.7 against the 2026-09-20 manual bag: at 3-6 m/s vertical accel 0.43/0.44/0.29 m/s^2 at 3-6/6-10/10-15 Hz (car 0.63/0.51/0.29), pitch rate 1.18/0.66/0.41 deg/s (car 1.23/0.87/0.37); at 9-12.5 m/s it is 20-30 % above the car (a_z 6-10 Hz 0.95 vs 0.73), the sim's motion growing faster with speed than the car's. 3x the level drove the car off the acceleration straight. The tyre grip load does not see the road. Gd0 0 turns it off.

Sensors._comment_imu: BMI088 as the car's uDV reads it: 400 Hz on a hardware timer, gyro ±2000 °/s (LSB 1.064 mrad/s, 1 kHz ODR, 116 Hz filter), accel ±6 g (LSB 1.796 mm/s²) at a 100 Hz ODR (ACC_CONF 0xA8), so each accel value repeats 4 times on /imu. /imu is not bias-corrected. Per-axis white noise is fitted from raw BMI088 logs (2026-09-29, 6 stationary power-ups, Allan deviation): accel 2.03/2.78/2.75 mm/s²/√Hz -> σ 0.018/0.025/0.025 m/s² per 100 Hz update (40 Hz filter), gyro 0.32/0.39/0.15 mrad/s/√Hz -> σ 0.0049/0.0059/0.0023 rad/s per 400 Hz sample (116 Hz filter); the gyro x/y values match the car's parked /imu (4.8/4.7 mrad/s). Turn-on gyro offsets were +1.8/+1.7/−0.7 mrad/s on the logger and −3.4/−1.1/−2.6 mrad/s in the 2026-09-20 car bag, so a fresh draw of σ 2.5 mrad/s per session; the car's |g| read 0.9 % low, so accel σ 0.05 m/s². AccelNoiseStd/GyroNoiseStd stay the scalars the bridge publishes as covariance, equal to uDV's (8.25e-4, 1.37e-5). In-run bias drift is still Ornstein–Uhlenbeck with τ 100 s: the logs are too short to fit it.

Imu._comment_vibration: On-car vibration, fitted to the car's /imu (manual bag 2026-09-20, 166 s at 3-12.5 m/s, minus the parked spectrum). The sim's physics ticks at ~60 Hz, so its chassis cannot make the car's 15-50 Hz content: a resonance near 23 Hz in a_z (1.35 m/s2 rms) and roll rate (0.06 rad/s), broader content in a_x / a_y. Per axis (REP-103 x/y/z): white noise through a bandpass at Hz / Q, scaled to Rms at VibrationRefSpeed, times min(v/VibrationOnSpeed, 1) * (max(v, OnSpeed)/RefSpeed)^VibrationSpeedExp (car: 10-45 Hz a_z 1.20 / 1.18 / 1.49 m/s2 at 3-6 / 6-9 / 9-12.5 m/s). The fit matches the car within 20-40 % per band from 10 to 50 Hz; below 10 Hz the sim's own chassis motion is left alone. Rms 0 = off.

Lidar1._comment_lidar: Hesai ATX_S01 datasheet (Section 1.4): 1-D rotating mirror (hybrid solid-state), 116 ch, 120° H × 18.3° V FoV (-12.4° to +5.9°), 10 Hz, ~1.74 M pts/s @ 0.08° H, 3 cm 1σ range. PointsPerSecond is the datasheet rate; the LiDAR stream is UDP-only since #322 (TCP and UDS senders retired — pre-#321 they existed to bypass macOS Docker Desktop's ~7 MB/s TCP loopback cap). At the full datasheet rate a ROS 2 subscriber receives the nominal 10.0 Hz on the GPU path (measured 2026-10-01); the ~7-8 Hz once attributed to DDS fragment loss matches the CPU path's own scan rate at this density (7.7-8.9 Hz). Sensor packs only emit *hits*, so the wire rate is roughly 65 % of attempted rays (e.g. 1.14 M pts/s of valid range returns at 1.74 M attempted).
Lidar1._comment_channel_elevations: Beam elevations of the car's Hesai in degrees, sensor frame, lowest first; PerChannelMaxRangeM uses the same order. Measured from the manual bag 2026-09-20: median elevation of each ring's returns over 30 parked scans (it varies by under 0.25° across the 120° sweep, from the mount's ~0.1° roll). The ATX spaces its beams unevenly: about 0.1° from -4° to +2.9° (two interleaved banks), 0.2° from -9° to -4° and from +2.9° to +4.6°, 0.4° above +4.6° and below -9°. With the -8.6° mount, cones beyond about 10 m fall in the sparse top beams, where a uniform 0.16° grid put 1.6-1.8x the car's beams on them. On the car the rings below about -10.7° are blocked by the nose and return almost nothing; 3 rings (62, 114, 115) never return, so they are spaced evenly between -10.67° and -12.80°. Without this array the sensor uses a uniform VerticalFOVLower..VerticalFOVUpper grid; with it, the V-FOV is taken from the table's ends.
Lidar1._comment_ring_ids: The car's ring number for each ChannelElevationsDeg entry above, same order. The car's Hesai numbers its beams in two interleaved banks (ring 0..63 from +5.8 to -12.8 deg, ring 64..115 from +2.9 to -12.3 deg), not by elevation; matched to the table within 0.004 deg on 113 rings (manual bag 2026-09-20), rings 62/114/115 have no returns there and take the three leftover entries by their bank's spacing. Used for the ring field of the organised /lidar_points.
Lidar1._comment_maxrange: MaxRange in metres. Real Hesai ATX_S01 spec is 200 m. Set to 30 m for the sim because cones past 30 m don't matter for FS detection (max-corridor-width is well under that), and shrinking the per-ray broadphase distance is the cheapest UE5 CPU optimisation we have — Chaos walks the spatial hash for every actor along the ray's path, so a 7× shorter ray cuts the per-ray work by roughly that factor. Bump back to 200 for benchmarks against real-car captures or non-FS scenarios.
Lidar1._comment_mount: Mount aligned with the IFS-08's actual LiDAR position: X=0 (CoG-aligned, just beneath the main hoop), Y=0 (centered), Z=1.10 m (main hoop crossbar height). Previously X=0.5 m / Z=0.9 m was a hood-mount approximation; correcting it shifts the sensor back ~50 cm and up ~20 cm, which changes both the cone-detection range envelope (cones at the rear become visible) and the time-to-first-detection for cones immediately ahead. Verify cone_detection still classifies cluster heights correctly after re-baselining.
Lidar1._comment_mount_pitch: Measured on the car (manual bag 2026-09-20, ground plane fitted to parked and driving scans): the Hesai sits 1.00-1.05 m above the ground, pitched 8.4-8.8 deg down, roll under 0.5 deg; a 60-scan fit gives 8.77 deg at 1.044 m. The sim mount took 8.6 until 2026-11-15; with it, a capture fitted the ground at 8.45 deg (the chassis sits slightly nose-up at rest). Pitch is the mount tilt in UE convention (negative = down); the 116 channels keep their -12.4..+5.9 deg spread in the sensor frame, so levelled they cover about -21..-2.7 deg and the ground is hit from ~3 m instead of ~5.3 m. Z=1.0 puts the sensor ~1.03 m above the ground: at Z=1.1 a 2026-11-02 sim capture measured 1.13 m.
Lidar1._comment_noise: Fitted to the car's Hesai (manual bag 2026-09-20, 40 parked scans, cells matched by ring and 0.1 deg azimuth): sigma = (RangeNoiseStd + RangeNoiseRangeCoeff*r^2) * (RangeNoiseRefReflectance/rho)^RangeNoiseReflectanceExp, clamped x0.3..x4. Car: 1.5 cm at 5-10 m, 1.9 cm at 10-15 m, 4.6-6.7 cm beyond 15 m; 4.5 cm on ~5 % reflectivity, 0.7 cm on ~45 %. EdgeSwapRate / EdgeDropRate: at a >30 cm depth edge to the neighbouring beam (left/right), the car (parked, 4-12 m) returns the other surface on ~15 % of edge returns, rarely anything in between, and edge beams return on ~73 % of scans against ~90 % inside a surface. IntensityNoise: relative jitter (car ~14 %).
Lidar1._comment_intensity: Intensity law fitted to the car's Hesai (manual bag 2026-09-20, 200 driving scans): whole numbers 0-255 that fall with range as r^-1.29 (cone faces at 10-25 cm height: 28 at 4 m, 11 at 10 m, 4-5 at 16-18 m) and do not depend on the angle of incidence (ground residual after the range law: cos^0.08). So I = IntensityScale * rho * r^-IntensityRangeExp, IntensityIncidenceExp 0, clamped to IntensityMax and rounded. IntensityScale 1460 puts the sim's blue cones (LUT rho 0.15) at I*r^1.29 ~ 215, near the car's median cone-like object (179), and the yellow ones (0.5) at ~ 700, near its upper decile (690); the car bag has no cone colours to check further. Surfaces with no LUT entry (asphalt, paint, scenery) take rho from scene luminance times a gain. The level's own floor renders at ~0.037, darker than asphalt: LuminanceReflectanceGain 3.2 lifts it to I*r^1.29 175, against the car's ground median of 183. A track's world (Montmeló) hides that floor and brings photo-matched colours: its asphalt at gain 1 gives ~160, so WorldLuminanceReflectanceGain is 1 (3.2 put it at 515). Remove IntensityScale for the old law (rho * cos * (5 m / r)^2, 0..1) and both gains for raw luminance.
Lidar1._comment_sweep: Mirror sweep measured on the car's Hesai (manual bag 2026-09-20): a scan is stamped at its first point, the rest follow over 89.8 ms, linear in azimuth (44.6 ms +/- 0.74 ms/deg), the same for every ring, and the direction reverses every scan. The car's driver does not motion-correct, so at 6-13 m/s static cones jump ~31 cm scan to scan (4 cm once each point is placed at its own time). The sim captures in one instant; SweepDurationMs moves each point by the car's motion over its delay so the sim's cloud smears the same way. 0 = one instant.
Lidar1._comment_dropout: Measured on the car's Hesai (manual bag 2026-09-20, parked, cells matched by ring and azimuth away from depth edges): returns drop out by strength, not at random. Ground cells return on 80 % of scans at intensity 0-2, 92 % at 2-8, 97-98 % at 8-32, 99 % above, so P(drop) = DropoutWeakRate * I^-DropoutWeakExp, capped at DropoutWeakMax, with I the noiseless intensity (0-255). A drop lasts: on cells missing 2-20 % of the time, a missing cell is missing again 1/2/4/8/16 same-direction scans later 65/58/50/42/30 % of the time, against 13 % if scans were independent. Each beam draws once per K same-direction scans, K log-uniform in [2, DropoutBurstScans] per beam; DropoutBurstIidShare of the probability is drawn fresh each scan. 64 / 0.15 give 67/53/36/22/12 % offline: right over the first few scans, short of the car's slow tail. DropoutRate is an extra flat per-ray rate, now 0 (it was 0.01). GPU path only.
Lidar1._comment_lidarpath: GPU path (#223): depth render of the scan envelope, async GPU→CPU readback, compute-shader decode. Default at the datasheet 1.74 M pts/s on every platform. Measured on Windows (RTX 3080, same track and driver): 10.0 Hz, sim 60 fps, readback 17 ms median / 34 ms p95 over PCIe, 4.3 cm mean cone position error. The CPU path ('cpu': ParallelFor + Chaos LineTraceSingleByChannel) is kept for parity checks only: at 1.74 M it reaches 7.7–8.9 Hz and smears each scan along the direction of travel (14 cm forward bias), and at 300 k pts/s (the v1.0.0 default) the detector misreads up to 11 % of small cones at 15–20 m as big orange, which trips the stop latch. Do not judge perception below the datasheet density.
Lidar1._comment_pointframe: Frame of /lidar_points. 'sensor' (the car's driver): origin at the LiDAR, axes tilted with the mount (Pitch above), so the ground sits ~1.03 m below and rises ahead at ~8.6 deg; the bridge publishes base_link -> hesai_lidar as the real mount pose, from getSensorOffset. 'vehicle' (the old default): points already levelled and moved to base_link, identity TF.
Lidar1._comment_perchannelmaxrange: Per-channel max-range overrides in METRES, indexed by V channel (0 = lowest V angle = -12.4°, 115 = highest = +5.9°). Real Hesai ATX_S01 has per-beam laser-power variance (datasheet App. A.1.1) — outer channels reach less far than central beams: 60 m bottom rings, 198 m centre, 90 m top. The array below is derived from the datasheet (App. A.1.2 Sorted by Ring IDs) and linearly remapped [60-198 m] → [25-30 m] so it fits under the sim's MaxRange=30 m perf budget while preserving the relative shape. Regenerate with `python3 tools/gen_per_channel_range.py --pretty`. Length must equal NumberOfChannels (116); mismatch logs a warning and falls back to MaxRange. Both CPU and GPU LiDAR paths read from this.
